messages:
Anya: FYI opened an escalation for Citrine Labs (org_id: org_8765). They report 'You don't have access' on Audit Logs UI even though they bought the 13mo retention addon and we show the entitlement enabled in Billing. Ticket INC-2345.

Eli: Can you paste repro steps and any console errors/screencaps?

Anya: Repro: login as customer admin via SSO -> navigate to Console > Compliance > Audit logs -> page shows a permissions banner 'You do not have access to view audit logs'. Other admin pages load. They tried an API call using their org API key and get 403. Snip of curl and response below:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_orgkey_XXXX" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/logs?org=org_8765"
# HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
# {
#   "error": "forbidden",
#   "message": "insufficient_scope",
#   "code": "audit_read"
# }
```

Anya: In our admin UI for org_8765 I see `audit_enabled: true` and `audit_retention_months: 13`. So weird. :thinking:

Sam: Two quick possibilities: 1) API key / token scope doesn't include `audit.read` (API key permissions model), or 2) SSO role->entitlement mapping didn't grant the `audit_logs_view` entitlement despite billing flag. Can you confirm whether the SSO group mapping includes the compliance role?

Anya: Customer says they are an Okta org and admins are in the `Redwood-Admins` group which maps to `admin` role. I checked org settings in billing and it shows the purchased plan + retention.

Eli: I'll check entitlement service and policies (OPA) for org_8765. Give me a minute to tail logs.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2345 created and auto-assigned to eng-sre. Priority: P2.

Eli: Pulled entitlement-service logs. There's an odd evaluation result: the policy engine returns deny with reason `unknown_compliance_profile`. Looks like this org retained `compliance_profile: legacy` during the 2024 entitlement migration and our fallback check skipped mapping to `audit_logs_view`. Paste of internal log line:

```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z entsvc[request-id=req_0a7f]: org=org_8765 evaluate_entitlements -> DENY {reason: "unknown_compliance_profile", profile: "legacy"}
```

Eli: Also confirmed API key check uses scopes from the `api_keys` table; keys for this org DO have `audit_read` present. So it's not the key scope. It's the entitlement evaluation path that denies UI/api access for users authenticated via SSO when the org has legacy profile.

Sam: That matches a migration gap we saw in Feb where ~0.8% of tenants kept the legacy profile tag. We patched later tenants but missed some during initial rollout.

Anya: Customer message draft: "We can see the billing flag for audit logs on the org but an internal migration marker is missing which prevents the UI from mapping your SSO roles to the Audit Logs viewer. We are escalating to our infra team and will enable a short-term fix." Thoughts?

Maya: That's good. Add an ETA for the fix and mention a workaround if safe (grant org-level `admin` role to the specific user) so they can access immediately.

Eli: For a short-term workaround we can flip the migration marker for org_8765 in internal admin: PATCH /internal/orgs/org_8765 {"audit_migration_complete": true} — this requires internal-admin token. I'll run that after we get sign-off. Longer-term: patch entitlement-service to fallback to billing flag when profile is legacy so we don't need manual flips.

Anya: Please hold on the manual patch until we confirm with security. Customer prefers not to have broad admin changes. I'll ask them if one admin can be temporarily elevated.

Sam: I'll approve the one-org manual marker change if Eli posts the exact DB/admin API call and tags me. Also want a quick audit after (list of actions, who changed what).

Eli: Command I'll run (internal-only):

```
# internal-admin only
PATCH https://internal-api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/org_8765
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"audit_migration_complete": true}
```

Eli: After applying, entitlement evaluation should re-run and grant `audit_logs_view` to mapped SSO roles. I can monitor logs and confirm.

Anya: Customer update queued: will propose 2 options: 1) short-term: temporary user elevation OR 2) we apply a manual migration marker (we need to confirm with security). Which do you prefer?

Maya: Offer both with our recommendation to use the manual marker so they don't need broad role changes. Mention ETA 1-2 hours for manual change + verification.

Sam: Approved. Eli, please add the change to the change-audit and ping me. Also run a quick sweep script to find other orgs with `compliance_profile: legacy` and put them in a reprocessing queue. I estimate ~12 orgs based on prior reports.

Eli: Will do. I've created a follow-up ticket ENG-ENT-408 for the entitlement-service fix to fallback to billing when profile=legacy. Linking it to INC-2345.

Anya: Great. I'll send the customer the draft message with the two options and tell them we're targeting 1-2 hours if they prefer our manual change.

ops-bot: INC-2345 updated: owner=Eli, status=in-progress, linked=ENG-ENT-408.

Sam: After this is closed, let's add a small console check so UI surfaces a clearer message when `unknown_compliance_profile` occurs (instead of generic 'You do not have access'). Customer-facing clarity will cut support load.

Anya: Agreed. Action items: Eli -> apply manual marker + run sweep + link audit. Sam -> approve and audit. Maya -> send customer comms. Anya -> update ticket. I'll post logs after Eli flips and close INC-2345 when customer confirms. :thumbsup:

Eli: Applying marker now, monitoring logs. (I'll paste result). :hourglass_flowing_sand:
